question: If frac{{(1 - cos theta )}}{{sin theta }} = (1)/(5), then what will be the value of frac{{(1 + cos theta )}}{{sin theta }}?
solution:
**Given:**

 frac{{(1 - cos θ )}}{{sin θ }} = (1)/(5)

**Concept used:**

cosec²θ - cot²θ = 1

cosec2θ - cot2θ = (cosecθ + cotθ)(cosecθ - cotθ)

**Calculation:**

 frac{{(1 - cos θ )}}{{sin θ }} = (1)/(5)

⇒ frac{{1}}{{sin θ }} - (cos θ)/(sinθ) = (1)/(5)

⇒ cosecθ - cotθ = (1)/(5)

Now,

(cosecθ + cotθ)(cosecθ - cotθ) = 1

⇒ (cosecθ + cotθ)(1)/(5) = 1

⇒ cosecθ + cotθ = 5

⇒ frac{{1}}{{sin θ }} + (cos θ)/(sinθ) = 5

⇒ frac{{(1 + cos theta )}}{{sin theta }} = 5

**∴ The required answer is 5.**
